_doc: Hand corrections applied by the VIEWER to the built tiles (pipeline/overrides.json is the pipeline's own; fold these into the pipeline on the next full rebuild: docs/TODO.md). Local metres (x east, z south). Every entry needs a 'why' and a 'source'. roadSurface: road id -> OSM-style surface (viewer/roadData.js SURFACE). plazas: paved open areas drawn as their own draped mesh (viewer/plazas.js) instead of the grass default; 'courseDeg' = direction of the stone rows (degrees from +x toward +z).

roadSurface._why: Was: the six roads named Place de Saint-Job forced to setts (2026-11-04). Corrected 2026-11-05: the owner checked on site that the ROADS round the Place, tram included, are asphalt with the grooved rails flush in it, as OSM says; the setts are on the SQUARE itself, which stands at sidewalk height with kerbs all round (UrbIS Land cover type P, drawn raised by viewer/surfaces.js with ?roads=surface; the plazas entry below for the default view).

plazas.why: Place de Saint-Job between the setts Chaussée (north) and Avenue du Prince de Ligne: one setts square with rows of plane trees and parking; OSM has no area for it, so it fell back to grass.
plazas.source: outline from the tile's roads.json (road centrelines); surface from the owner's photos 2026-11-04

plazas.why: Place de Saint-Job between Avenue du Prince de Ligne and the Place streets in front of the church (kiosk, terraces): setts.
plazas.source: outline from roads.json; surface from the owner's photos 2026-11-04

flyStart.why: Fly mode starts just above the tip of the Saint-Job church spire (its highest vertex in G4 buildings.bin: 1201.64, 130.25, 549.25), heading over Place de Saint-Job (owner, 2026-11-04).

centreLine._why: Rue Edith Cavell (OSM tertiary -> engine type 'collector') got the type's default dashed centre line; the measured-paint rule removes guessed centre lines on residential types only. The 2024 orthophoto shows no centre line along it (checked at (569, -1300), (540, -1040), (600, -760), (632, -640): parking bays on both sides, a SCHOOL legend, no line), and UrbIS Topo has none. Keys: OSM way ids (every piece rWAY_n of the way).
centreLine._source: UrbIS orthophoto 2024 (CC0), looked at in roads round 5 (2026-11-13)

parkSquares.name: Square des Heros
parkSquares.why: UrbIS maps the whole square (lawns, dolomite paths, the war memorial's terrace) as one street surface of class 'square': the tiles drew it as a raised setts plaza. The park itself (OSM way 23542633) is the hero place's own ground (viewer/heros/); the strip of the surface round it stays, as sidewalk paving.
parkSquares.source: UrbIS StreetSurfaces 40047 minus OSM leisure=park w23542633; Commons / heritage.uccle.be photos (docs/landmarks/HEROS.md)

bridgePlans._doc: OSM way id of a road tagged bridge=yes -> its deck's measured outline (viewer/streets/bridgeDecks.js plan decks; ?bridgeplan=old = the road band). ring: [x, z] outline; free: indices of ring edges that span the cutting (fascia, no wall); walls: the cutting walls under the deck; under: the station floor between them (terrain cut to level).

1342926162._why: The NEW Carsoel deck over Saint-Job station (old 1928 S-curve bridge demolished Jan 2025, new straight deck open to trams 2 June 2025): ~45 m along the railway (29 precast 15 m beams), the road diagonally across it, the tram 92 stop 'Gare de Saint-Job' and bus platforms on it, widened sidewalks with small green beds. The road band of bridgeDecks.js left the platforms, shelters and sidewalks hanging over the cutting (owner playtest 2026-11-16).
1342926162.source: Outline from OSM 2025 (bridge=yes ways 1342926162, 1411905486/88, 1411869726/27/57/58, 1411916284/87/88, stairs 1412205415/17 to the train platforms), the UrbIS orthophoto (construction slab, H6) and the DTM 2021 cutting; L'Avenir 2024-07-15 / Bx1 2025-06 (45 m wide deck, 15 m beams, road diagonal, tram stop on the deck). Axis frame: c = between the two L26 tracks at x 899.6, u along the line.
1342926162._ring: Both ends overlap the UrbIS street polygons by ~1.5 m (the deck top tucks 10 cm under the drawn street there) of Avenue Carsoel exactly (west: tram road be/id/streetsurface/17109 and sidewalks 134927 / 132971, which already have the new layout; east: 28868, 132776, 132777), so the measured street continues the deck without overlap; the north edge at the east end (railed) is the sidewalk's back edge over the opened cutting (the 1928 bridge's site).

bank.why: claude/footbridge (TODO 2026-11-17 'Saint-Job deck sidewalks over the bank', rule deck-covers-street): the Rue de la Pecherie / Carsoel sidewalk (UrbIS be/id/streetsurface/134927 + the tram road 17109's corner) runs on past the hand ring's west edge over the cutting's south-west bank; the street stage draped it on the bare DTM there (1-5 m over the slope, deckJoins 'street step at the joint' 0.66-0.71 m). The ring widened west to the sidewalk's back edge (x 870.6, z 529.6), its new north-west edge a wing wall into the bank with the railing over the drop. ?footbridge=old: the hand ring.

bridgeProfiles._doc: OSM road bridges' measured top along the centre line (tools/bridges/deckProfiles.py, rule deck-profile-measured): [x, z, y, ...] every 2 m, m TAW. viewer/streets/bridgeDecks.js bridgeDescriptors draws the deck's profile through it (?bridgeprof=old: the straight line between the ends' ground).

buildingLooks._doc: UrbIS solid id -> { style (facades.js wall styles: 0 red brick, 1 brown, 2 yellow, 3 white render, 4 cream, 5 grey), roofColor (linear rgb; red-orange = clay tiles), bayScale [s, nx, nz] (the face facing (nx, nz) lays its painted window grid out in u x s: a narrow front with more windows than the 2.6 m bays give; facadeGeom.js) }: the looks a local recognises, each checked on Street View (look only). ?looks=old: none. type (viewer/buildingTypes.js TYPE: 0 generic, 1 maison de maitre, 2 art deco / modernist, 3 bel-etage, 4 block, 5 villa), garage false (no garage door), true (a garage door the classifier did not give). cortenbosch2 (docs/CORTENBOSCH2.md): type 6 = the 1990s house { tone buff|salmon|cream|orange|brown, frame white|brown|anthracite, fascia cream|stained|fibre }, type 7 = the glass curtain wall { grid burgundy|anthracite|silver|green, spandrel glass|metal|grey }; roofTile 'concrete' (interlocking concrete tiles, any type); v2: fields over the entry under round 2 (?cortenbosch2=old: without them); set 'cortenbosch2': only with round 2.

gardenRestyle._doc: Polygons (city x, z) where the generated front-garden pieces (viewer/gardens/cityGardens.js: brick walls, railings, pillars, driveway gates) are what a local would NOT see: inside, every wall / railing run becomes a clipped hedge of `hedge` (gardenHedge.js species) `height` m high, set back off the street, the pillars and gates go (the driveways stay open). ?cortenbosch=old: none.

papenkasteel_hedge_south.why: claude/places2: the Papenkasteel's grounds on Rue Papenkasteel are closed by a tall clipped beech / hornbeam hedge (~2.1 m) right behind the narrow verge, trees over it, broken only by the castle's street gate (white-render piers, black iron double gate: data/parkfence/papenkasteel.obs.json); the garden kit plans hedges for house fronts only and drew nothing on this frontage

cortenbosch_old_lane.why: Chemin privé 't Cortenbosch's old lane (setts, ~3 m, between n. 5 and Avenue du Lycée Français): green banks, overgrown hedges and conifers, a dark green metal railing, a few low white picket gates; no brick walls with pillars (the kit drew red-brick walls, white pillars and black iron gates)

cortenbosch_lane.why: Chemin privé 't Cortenbosch's 1990s part: every plot is closed by a clipped beech hedge (copper-brown leaves held all winter; a few ivy hedges), open driveways, no walls, no brick pillars, no iron gates (the kit drew red-brick walls, pillars and black gates)

grounds.why: claude/carrefour2 (owner 2026-11-24: 'same design as Carrefour Market Marlow'; its car park is at ground level): the Carrefour Market Rue Gatti de Gamond 60's asphalt car park, an L round the store: the big part between the glazed front and Avenue Docteur Decroly (a long row of bays nose-in along the street hedge, then five islands of bays square to the front, two of them double with small trees between, two disabled bays by the entrance, painted arrows, a zebra walk from the Decroly sidewalk straight to the entrance) and a strip along the store's east wall (two rows of bays facing each other); entered from Rue Gatti de Gamond by a curved drive at the store's south-west corner past a hatched island, the in / out on Avenue Docteur Decroly at the south-east corner between yellow-and-black bollards; a black mesh fence on a low clipped hedge along the Decroly sidewalk, dark green lantern lamp posts, red round trolley signs on poles; two trolley shelters in red and white (a white metal roof on a red band: a long one at the west end, a short one by the zebra walk; not drawn); the city drew a lawn crossed by paths
grounds.source: Google Street View Apr 2024 (look only, 2026-11-24) + UrbIS orthophoto 2024 (CC0, 10 cm: the lot's outline and its 12 bay rows read off it); the north edge is the store's footprint (UrbIS solid 558122), the west edge the Gatti de Gamond sidewalk, the south edge the back of the street row of bays, the east edge the hedge

roadTexts._doc: Words painted on a street (viewer/streets/measuredPaint.js roadTextMesh, viewer/roadPaint.js roadTextMaterial): id -> { at [x, z] the first line's centre, dir [dx, dz] the reader's way (the nearest line first), lines, w across (m), h each line along (m), gap (m); along true: each line runs along dir (letters' tops to its left), the lines side by side, at = their centre, L = a line's length, h its height; why, source }; draped on the measured street's markable triangles like the measured paint. ?cortenbosch2=old: none.

chenaie.why: owner playtest: 'the children's garden in front of Le Pigeon Noir'. Across Avenue de la Chênaie from the restaurant: a small public garden (OSM park 1123840941) behind an angled parking row on setts and a low clipped hedge: a sand playground (OSM 1123841132, surface sand) with natural timber play frames (log climbing frames with rope nets, a balance frame, a small timber tower), a lawn, a gravel path, park benches and bins, young globe-crowned trees, a lamp post, two boules pitches to the south. Not a fenced kindergarten: the garden is open. The city drew the sand and the benches but no equipment (the playground kit was only in the lab). (claude/places3) drawn with the timber kit made for it (tools/blender/timberPlayKit.py): a small log tower with a rope net, a log climbing frame with two rope nets, a balance course of logs on stumps; piecesOld = the playground kit's plastic stand-ins drawn before (?parkpieces=old)
chenaie.source: Google Street View Apr 2024 from Avenue de la Chênaie 5 (look only, 2026-11-23)
